provisions.summary: The Regulation sets sustainability, safety, labelling, marking and information requirements that batteries must meet to be placed on the market or put into service in the Union, minimum rules on extended producer responsibility, collection, treatment and reporting for waste batteries, due diligence obligations for economic operators placing batteries on the market or putting them into service, and green public procurement requirements.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries; economic operators
provisions.applicable_from: 2024-02-18 (general application, Art. 96), subject to later dates in individual provisions

provisions.summary: Applies to all categories of batteries - portable batteries, SLI batteries, LMT batteries, electric vehicle batteries and industrial batteries - whatever their shape, volume, weight, design, material composition, chemistry, use or purpose, including batteries incorporated into or added to products or designed for that. For Chapter II, a battery that could fall under more than one category is treated as belonging to the category with the strictest requirements.
provisions.applies_to: All battery categories
provisions.conditions: The strictest-category rule is worded for Chapter II (sustainability and safety) only, not for Chapter III (labelling) or Chapter IX (passport).

provisions.summary: Battery cells or modules made available for end use without further incorporation or assembly into larger packs or batteries count as batteries placed on the market and must meet the requirements of the most similar category; where more than one category could apply, the strictest applies.
provisions.applies_to: Battery cells and modules sold for end use

provisions.summary: The Regulation does not apply to batteries incorporated into, or specifically designed to be incorporated into, (a) equipment connected with the protection of Member States' essential security interests, arms, munitions and war material, other than products not intended for specifically military purposes, or (b) equipment designed to be sent into space.
provisions.applies_to: Military and space equipment batteries
provisions.conditions: Full exclusion from the Regulation

provisions.version_examined: Consolidated version 02023R1542-20260813, as corrected by corrigendum OJ L, 2024/90243, 17.4.2024 (original OJ text read 'Chapters III and VIII')
provisions.summary: Chapters III (labelling, marking and information) and IX (digital battery passport) do not apply to equipment specifically designed for the safety of nuclear installations as defined in Article 3 of Directive 2009/71/Euratom.
provisions.applies_to: Equipment for the safety of nuclear installations
provisions.conditions: Partial exclusion: only Chapters III and IX. An engine built from the uncorrected 2023 OJ text would wrongly exclude Chapter VIII instead of Chapter IX.

provisions.summary: 'Battery': a device delivering electrical energy generated by direct conversion of chemical energy, with internal or external storage, consisting of one or more non-rechargeable or rechargeable cells, modules or packs; it includes a battery that has been prepared for re-use, prepared for repurposing, repurposed or remanufactured. Points (2), (3) and (4) define battery pack, battery module and battery cell.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries

provisions.summary: 'Portable battery': a sealed battery weighing 5 kg or less, not designed specifically for industrial use, and neither an electric vehicle battery, an LMT battery nor an SLI battery.
provisions.applies_to: Portable batteries
provisions.conditions: Threshold: weight of 5 kg or less

provisions.summary: 'Portable battery of general use': a portable battery, rechargeable or not, specifically designed to be interoperable and having one of the common formats 4,5 V (3R12), button cell, D, C, AA, AAA, AAAA, A23 or 9 V (PP3).
provisions.applies_to: Portable batteries of general use
provisions.conditions: Closed list of formats

provisions.summary: 'Light means of transport battery' or 'LMT battery': a sealed battery weighing 25 kg or less, specifically designed to provide electric power for the traction of wheeled vehicles that can be powered by an electric motor alone or by a combination of motor and human power, including type-approved category L vehicles under Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, and that is not an electric vehicle battery.
provisions.applies_to: LMT batteries
provisions.conditions: Thresholds: sealed; 25 kg or less; wheeled vehicles only

provisions.summary: 'Starting, lighting and ignition battery' or 'SLI battery': a battery specifically designed to supply electric power for starting, lighting or ignition, which can also be used for auxiliary or backup purposes in vehicles, other means of transport or machinery.
provisions.applies_to: SLI batteries
provisions.conditions: No weight or capacity threshold

provisions.summary: 'Industrial battery': a battery specifically designed for industrial uses, or intended for industrial uses after preparation for repurposing or repurposing, or any other battery weighing more than 5 kg that is neither an electric vehicle battery, an LMT battery nor an SLI battery.
provisions.applies_to: Industrial batteries
provisions.conditions: Residual category for batteries over 5 kg. The 2 kWh capacity threshold is not part of this definition; it appears in the operative provisions (Art. 7, 8, 10, 13(6), 77(1)).

provisions.summary: 'Electric vehicle battery': a battery specifically designed to provide electric power for traction in hybrid or electric vehicles of category L under Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 and weighing more than 25 kg, or a battery specifically designed to provide electric power for traction in hybrid or electric vehicles of categories M, N or O under Regulation (EU) 2018/858.
provisions.applies_to: Electric vehicle batteries
provisions.conditions: Category L: more than 25 kg; categories M, N, O: no weight threshold

provisions.summary: 'Stationary battery energy storage system': an industrial battery with internal storage specifically designed to store and deliver electric energy from and into the grid or to end-users, regardless of where and by whom it is used.
provisions.applies_to: Stationary battery energy storage systems (sub-category of industrial batteries)

provisions.summary: 'Placing on the market' is the first making available of a battery on the Union market. 'Making available on the market' is any supply of a battery for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries; economic operators

provisions.summary: 'Putting into service' is the first use, for its intended purpose, in the Union, of a battery without it having been placed on the market previously.
provisions.applies_to: Batteries used without prior placing on the market (for example own use)
provisions.conditions: Applies only where there was no previous placing on the market

provisions.summary: 'Battery model': a version of a battery of which all units share the same technical characteristics relevant for the requirements of the Regulation on sustainability, safety, labelling, marking and information, and the same model identifier.
provisions.applies_to: Model-level data sets

provisions.summary: 'Economic operator' means the manufacturer, the authorised representative, the importer, the distributor, the fulfilment service provider or any other natural or legal person subject to obligations in relation to batteries under the Regulation. 'Manufacturer' means a person who manufactures a battery or has one designed or manufactured and markets it under its own name or trademark or puts it into service for its own purposes.
provisions.applies_to: Actors
provisions.conditions: Points (63), (64), (65) define authorised representative, importer and distributor; fulfilment service provider is imported from Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 by Art. 3(2)(b).

provisions.summary: 'QR code' means a machine-readable matrix code that links to information required by the Regulation.
provisions.applies_to: Data carrier

provisions.summary: 'Unique identifier' means a unique string of characters for the identification of batteries that also enables a web link to the battery passport.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport identifier
provisions.conditions: Art. 3(1) has 68 points. There is no separate Art. 3 definition of 'battery passport' (it is defined in-line in Art. 77(1) as an electronic record), nor of 'battery category', 'capacity' or 'rated capacity'.

provisions.summary: 'State of health' is a measure of the general condition of a rechargeable battery and its ability to deliver the specified performance compared with its initial condition. 'Preparation for re-use' takes the Directive 2008/98/EC meaning. 'Preparation for repurposing' is an operation by which a waste battery or parts of it are prepared for a different purpose than the original one. 'Repurposing' is an operation resulting in a battery that is not waste, or parts of it, being used for a different purpose than the original one. 'Remanufacturing' is a technical operation on a used battery involving disassembly and evaluation of all cells and modules and use of new, used or recovered cells, modules or components to restore capacity to at least 90 % of the original rated capacity, with state of health of cells not differing by more than 3 %, for the same purpose as originally designed.
provisions.applies_to: Battery status changes
provisions.conditions: Remanufacturing thresholds: at least 90 % of original rated capacity; cell state-of-health spread within 3 %

provisions.summary: A carbon footprint declaration is required for each battery model per manufacturing plant for electric vehicle batteries, rechargeable industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and LMT batteries. It applies from the later of a fixed date and a period after entry into force of the methodology delegated act or the declaration-format implementing act: (a) EV: 18 February 2025 or 12 months; (b) rechargeable industrial except those with exclusively external storage: 18 February 2026 or 18 months; (c) LMT: 18 August 2028 or 18 months; (d) rechargeable industrial with external storage: 18 August 2030 or 18 months. Until accessible through the QR code, the declaration accompanies the battery. The Commission is to adopt the delegated act on methodology and the implementing act on format by 18 February 2024 (EV), 18 February 2025, 18 February 2027 and 18 February 2029 respectively.
provisions.applies_to: EV batteries; rechargeable industrial batteries > 2 kWh; LMT batteries
provisions.applicable_from: Later of the fixed date per category and 12 or 18 months after entry into force of the delegated or implementing act
provisions.conditions: No adopted Art. 7 delegated or implementing act was located as of 2026-10-13, so no category's declaration date can be fixed. Art. 7(5): does not apply to batteries prepared for re-use, prepared for repurposing, repurposed or remanufactured if already placed on the market or put into service before.

provisions.summary: Para 2: the same categories must bear a label showing the carbon footprint and the performance class, from the later of 18 August 2026 (EV), 18 August 2027 (rechargeable industrial except exclusively external storage), 18 February 2030 (LMT), 18 February 2032 (industrial with external storage) and 18 months after entry into force of the relevant delegated or implementing act. Para 3: the technical documentation must show the footprint is below a maximum threshold set by delegated act, from the later of 18 February 2028 (EV), 18 February 2029, 18 August 2031 and 18 August 2033 and 18 months after entry into force of that delegated act.
provisions.applies_to: EV batteries; rechargeable industrial batteries > 2 kWh; LMT batteries
provisions.applicable_from: Later of the fixed date per category and 18 months after entry into force of the relevant act
provisions.conditions: Depends on delegated acts (performance classes, maximum thresholds) and an implementing act (label format); none located as adopted.

provisions.summary: From the later of 18 August 2028 and 24 months after entry into force of the methodology delegated act, industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh (except those with exclusively external storage), electric vehicle batteries and SLI batteries containing cobalt, lead, lithium or nickel in active materials must be accompanied by documentation on the share of those materials recovered from battery manufacturing waste or post-consumer waste (lead: recovered from waste), per battery model per year and per manufacturing plant. The same applies to LMT batteries from 18 August 2033. The Commission is to adopt the methodology delegated act by 18 August 2026.
provisions.applies_to: Industrial batteries > 2 kWh (except exclusively external storage); EV batteries; SLI batteries; LMT batteries (from 2033)
provisions.applicable_from: Later of 2028-08-18 and 24 months after entry into force of the Art. 8(1) delegated act; LMT from 2033-08-18
provisions.conditions: Delegated act not located as adopted. Art. 8(4): not applicable to batteries prepared for re-use, repurposed or remanufactured if previously placed on the market or put into service. Art. 8(2)-(3) minimum shares apply from 18 August 2031 (16 % cobalt, 85 % lead, 6 % lithium, 6 % nickel) and 18 August 2036 (26 %, 85 %, 12 %, 15 %).

provisions.summary: From 18 August 2024, rechargeable industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh, LMT batteries and electric vehicle batteries must be accompanied by a document containing values for the electrochemical performance and durability parameters in Part A of Annex IV; the technical documentation explains the specifications, standards and conditions used, with the elements in Part B of Annex IV.
provisions.applies_to: Rechargeable industrial batteries > 2 kWh; LMT batteries; EV batteries
provisions.conditions: Already applicable, so it is not a later-date dependency for Annex XIII point 4(a). Art. 10(2)-(3) minimum values depend on delegated acts (deadlines 18 February 2026 and 18 February 2027) and apply from the later of 18 August 2027 / 18 August 2028 and 18 months after those acts. Art. 10(4): exemption for batteries prepared for re-use etc. if the operator shows prior placing on the market.

provisions.summary: Batteries must bear a label containing the general information set out in Part A of Annex VI.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries
provisions.applicable_from: Later of 2026-08-18 and 18 months after the entry into force of the implementing act referred to in Art. 13(10) ('whichever is the latest')
provisions.conditions: No adopted Art. 13(10) implementing act was located as of 2026-10-13 (a draft was notified to the WTO in December 2025). The date therefore cannot be fixed, and it cannot be earlier than 18 months after a future entry into force.

provisions.summary: Rechargeable portable batteries, LMT batteries and SLI batteries must bear a label with information on their capacity.
provisions.applies_to: Rechargeable portable batteries; LMT batteries; SLI batteries
provisions.applicable_from: Same formula as Art. 13(1): later of 2026-08-18 and 18 months after entry into force of the Art. 13(10) implementing act
provisions.conditions: Depends on the Art. 13(10) implementing act (not located as adopted)

provisions.summary: Non-rechargeable portable batteries must bear a label with their minimum average duration when used in specific applications and a label indicating 'non-rechargeable'.
provisions.applies_to: Non-rechargeable portable batteries
provisions.conditions: Depends on the Art. 13(10) implementing act (not located as adopted)

provisions.summary: All batteries must be marked with the separate-collection symbol in Part B of Annex VI. The symbol covers at least 3 % of the area of the largest side up to 5 x 5 cm; for cylindrical cells at least 1,5 % of the surface area up to 5 x 5 cm; where the symbol would be smaller than 0,47 x 0,47 cm the battery need not be marked and a symbol of at least 1 x 1 cm is printed on the packaging.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries
provisions.conditions: Fixed date; no dependency on an implementing act

provisions.summary: Batteries containing more than 0,002 % cadmium or more than 0,004 % lead must be marked with the chemical symbol Cd or Pb, printed beneath the separate-collection symbol and covering at least one quarter of that symbol's size.
provisions.applies_to: Batteries above the cadmium or lead thresholds
provisions.applicable_from: No date stated in the paragraph (re-checked: it opens 'All batteries containing ...'); general application 2024-02-18 applies
provisions.conditions: Thresholds: > 0,002 % Cd; > 0,004 % Pb. Placement is defined relative to the Art. 13(4) separate-collection symbol, which is itself only required from 2025-08-18; Chapter VI manufacturer duties on Art. 13 marking apply from 2024-08-18. The effective start date for a rule check is therefore a matter of interpretation and should not be hard-coded without review.

provisions.summary: All batteries must be marked with a QR code as described in Part C of Annex VI. The QR code gives access to: (a) for LMT batteries, industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and electric vehicle batteries, the battery passport under Art. 77; (b) for other batteries, the applicable information in paragraphs 1 to 5, the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 18), the due diligence report (Art. 52(3)) and the waste prevention and management information in Art. 74(1), points (a) to (f); (c) for SLI batteries, the amount of cobalt, lead, lithium or nickel recovered from waste and present in active materials, calculated under Art. 8. The information must be complete, up to date and accurate.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries, with content depending on category
provisions.conditions: Fixed date. Content items inherit their own dates: Art. 52(3) report only once due diligence applies (2027-08-18, and subject to Art. 47); SLI recycled-content amount only once Art. 8(1) applies.

provisions.summary: Labels and the QR code must be printed or engraved visibly, legibly and indelibly on the battery; where that is not possible or not warranted because of the nature and size of the battery, they are affixed to the packaging and to the documents accompanying the battery.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries

provisions.summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts to amend the Regulation to provide for alternative types of smart labels instead of, or in addition to, the QR code, in view of technical and scientific progress.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: No such delegated act located

provisions.summary: Batteries that have been prepared for re-use, prepared for repurposing, repurposed or remanufactured must bear new labels or be marked with new markings under Art. 13 containing information on their change of status in accordance with point 4 of Annex XIII, accessible through the QR code.
provisions.applies_to: Re-used, repurposed and remanufactured batteries
provisions.applicable_from: No date stated in the paragraph
provisions.conditions: Cross-refers to Annex XIII point 4 (individual battery data, including status)

provisions.summary: By 18 August 2025 the Commission is to adopt implementing acts establishing harmonised specifications for the labelling requirements in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3, under the examination procedure of Art. 90(3).
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: Adopted act not located as of 2026-10-13; draft notified to the WTO (G/TBT/N/EU/1181, arrival 2025-12-22).

provisions.summary: General information on the label, ten points: (1) manufacturer identification per Art. 38(7); (2) battery category and identification information per Art. 38(6); (3) place of manufacture (geographical location of the manufacturing plant); (4) date of manufacture (month and year); (5) weight; (6) capacity; (7) chemistry; (8) hazardous substances present other than mercury, cadmium or lead; (9) usable extinguishing agent; (10) critical raw materials present in a concentration of more than 0,1 % weight by weight.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries (label); battery passport point 1(a) for passport categories
provisions.applicable_from: As a label: Art. 13(1) date. As passport content: 2027-02-18 via Art. 77 and Annex XIII point 1(a)
provisions.conditions: The label date and the passport date are different triggers for the same data set.

provisions.citation: Annex VI, Parts B and C
provisions.summary: Part B shows the symbol for separate collection of batteries (an image). Part C requires the QR code to have a high colour contrast with the background and a size easily readable by a commonly available QR reader, such as those integrated in hand-held communication devices. Part C names no symbology standard.
provisions.applies_to: All batteries
provisions.conditions: For passport categories Art. 77(3) adds the ISO/IEC 15459 requirement to the QR code and unique identifier.

provisions.summary: From 18 August 2024 the battery management system of stationary battery energy storage systems, LMT batteries and electric vehicle batteries must contain up-to-date data on the state-of-health and expected-lifetime parameters in Annex VII; read-only access is given to the legal purchaser or a third party acting on their behalf. Annex VII Part A: for EV batteries, state of certified energy (SOCE); for stationary systems and LMT batteries, remaining capacity and, where possible, remaining power capability, remaining round-trip efficiency, evolution of self-discharge rates and ohmic resistance. Part B (stationary systems and LMT batteries): manufacture and putting-into-service dates, energy throughput, capacity throughput, tracking of harmful events, number of full equivalent charge-discharge cycles.
provisions.applies_to: Stationary battery energy storage systems; LMT batteries; EV batteries
provisions.conditions: Already applicable, so it is not a later-date dependency for Annex XIII point 4(b). Industrial batteries other than stationary storage systems are outside Art. 14.

provisions.summary: Art. 15(1) sets quality criteria for tests, measurements and calculations used to verify compliance with Articles 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and 78, including harmonised standards referenced in the Official Journal. Art. 17 assigns conformity assessment modules: Articles 6, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 14 use Module A or D1 (series) or Module A or G (non-series); Articles 7 and 8 use Module D1 (series) or G (non-series); batteries that underwent preparation for re-use, repurposing or remanufacturing get an additional Module A assessment. Art. 18: the EU declaration of conformity states compliance with Articles 6 to 10, 12, 13 and 14, follows Annex IX, is electronic and is translated as required by the Member State.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers; all batteries
provisions.conditions: Chapter IX (Art. 77-78) is not listed among the articles covered by the declaration of conformity; Art. 78 is listed in Art. 15(1).

provisions.summary: Manufacturers, when placing a battery on the market or putting it into service including for their own purposes, ensure it is marked and labelled under Art. 13; batteries bear a model identification and a batch or serial number or other identifying element (para 6) and the manufacturer's name, trade name or trademark, postal address and, if available, web and email address (para 7). Operators that place on the market batteries prepared for re-use, prepared for repurposing, repurposed or remanufactured are treated as manufacturers (para 11). Importers (Art. 41(2)) and distributors (Art. 42(2)) verify, among other things, that the battery is marked and labelled under Art. 13.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers; importers; distributors
provisions.conditions: These paragraphs do not mention the battery passport.

provisions.summary: Operators placing on the market or putting into service batteries that underwent preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing ensure quality control and safety during examination, testing, packing and shipment, ensure compliance with the Regulation and other Union product, environmental, health and transport law taking account that the battery may now fall under a different category, and for remanufacturing provide documentation to market surveillance authorities on request.
provisions.applies_to: Second-life operators
provisions.conditions: A status change can change the battery category and therefore the passport and QR obligations.

provisions.summary: Chapter VII (due diligence) does not apply to economic operators with a net turnover of less than EUR 40 million in the financial year preceding the last financial year, unless they are part of a group of parent and subsidiary undertakings exceeding EUR 40 million on a consolidated basis; nor to operators for batteries prepared for re-use, prepared for repurposing, repurposed or remanufactured if the batteries were already placed on the market or put into service before.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operators placing batteries on the market or putting them into service
provisions.conditions: Threshold EUR 40 million net turnover (group consolidation rule). A pending proposal (2025/0130(COD)) may change this; not law as of 2026-10-13.

provisions.version_examined: Consolidated version 02023R1542-20260813, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/1561 (M2)
provisions.summary: From 18 August 2027, economic operators placing batteries on the market or putting them into service must fulfil the due diligence obligations in Art. 48(2)-(3), 49, 50 and 52 and set up due diligence policies. By 26 July 2026 the Commission is to publish guidelines on the application of the due diligence requirements in Articles 49 and 50.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operators above the Art. 47 threshold
provisions.conditions: Both dates carry the M2 marker. Guidelines not located as published.

provisions.summary: The economic operator reviews and publishes annually, including on the internet, a report on its battery due diligence policy, easily comprehensible for end-users and clearly identifying the batteries concerned, covering steps taken under Articles 49 and 50, significant adverse impacts found and how they were addressed, and a summary of third-party verifications including the name of the notified body.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operators above the Art. 47 threshold
provisions.conditions: This report is the source of Annex XIII point 1(d) and of Art. 13(6)(b).

provisions.summary: From 18 February 2027 each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service shall have an electronic record, called the battery passport.
provisions.applies_to: LMT batteries; industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh; electric vehicle batteries
provisions.conditions: Threshold wording: 'industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh' (strictly greater than; applies to industrial batteries only - LMT and EV have no capacity threshold). Trigger: placed on the market OR put into service on or after the date. Granularity: one passport per individual battery ('each'). Not covered: portable batteries, SLI batteries, industrial batteries of 2 kWh or less. Excluded by Art. 1(5)-(6): military, space and nuclear-safety equipment.

provisions.summary: The passport contains information relating to the battery model and information specific to the individual battery, including information resulting from its use, as set out in Annex XIII. Three access groups: (a) the general public - point 1 of Annex XIII; (b) only notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission - points 2 and 3; (c) only natural or legal persons with a legitimate interest - points 2 and 4, for the purposes of (a) dismantling, including safety measures, and detailed composition, where essential for repairers, remanufacturers, second-life operators and recyclers, or (b) for individual batteries, where essential to the purchaser or parties acting on its behalf for making the battery available to independent energy aggregators or energy market participants. The information is included to the extent applicable to the category or sub-category of battery concerned.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport data set and access control
provisions.conditions: Category applicability filter is explicit in the text. The detailed list of persons with a legitimate interest depends on the Art. 77(9) implementing act (not located as adopted).

provisions.summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Art. 89 to amend Annex XIII as regards the information to be included in the battery passport, in view of technical and scientific progress.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: No delegated act amending Annex XIII located; the only change to Annex XIII found is corrigendum C4.

provisions.summary: The passport is accessible through the QR code of Art. 13(6), which links to a unique identifier that the economic operator placing the battery on the market attributes to it. The QR code and the unique identifier must comply with ISO/IEC 15459-1:2014, 15459-2:2015, 15459-3:2014, 15459-4:2014, 15459-5:2014 and 15459-6:2014 or their equivalent. The Commission may by delegated act replace those standards or add other European or international standards.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the battery on the market; QR code and unique identifier
provisions.conditions: Dated editions are named in the enacting text; 'or their equivalent' leaves room for other schemes. The identifier is attributed by the operator 'placing the battery on the market' (putting into service is not named in this paragraph).

provisions.summary: The economic operator placing the battery on the market ensures that the information in the battery passport is accurate, complete and up to date; it may give written authorisation to any other operator to act on its behalf.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the battery on the market
provisions.conditions: Recital 125 adds that responsibility stays with the operator placing the battery on the market even where another party updates the passport under authorisation.

provisions.summary: All passport information must be based on open standards, in an interoperable format, transferable through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in, machine-readable, structured and searchable, in line with the essential requirements of Art. 78. Access to the information is regulated in accordance with those essential requirements.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport data format and access

provisions.summary: For a battery that has been subject to preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing, responsibility for the Art. 77(4) obligations transfers to the economic operator that placed that battery on the market or put it into service; such a battery has a new battery passport linked to the passport or passports of the original battery or batteries. Where a battery's status changes to waste, responsibility transfers to the producer or, where appointed under Art. 57(1), the producer responsibility organisation, or the waste management operator selected under Art. 57(8).
provisions.applies_to: Second-life operators; producers; producer responsibility organisations; waste management operators
provisions.conditions: New passport required and it must link to the original passport(s); the many-to-one case (several original batteries) is expressly contemplated.

provisions.summary: A battery passport ceases to exist after the battery has been recycled.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport lifecycle

provisions.summary: By 18 August 2026 the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying which persons are to be considered persons with a legitimate interest as referred to in points 2 and 4 of Annex XIII for the purposes of Art. 77(2)(c), to which information listed in those points they have access, and to what extent they can download, share, publish and re-use it; examination procedure of Art. 90(3). provisions.summary: Essential requirements for the technical design and operation of the battery passport: (a) full interoperability with other digital product passports required by Union law on ecodesign, as regards technical, semantic and organisational aspects of end-to-end communication and data transfer; (b) free access for consumers, economic operators and other relevant actors according to their access rights under Annex XIII and the Art. 77(9) implementing act; (c) data stored by the economic operator responsible under Art. 77(4) and (7) or by operators authorised to act on its behalf; (d) authorised operators may not sell, re-use or process the data beyond what is necessary for the storage or processing service; (e) the passport remains available after the responsible operator ceases to exist or ceases its activity in the Union; (f) rights to access, introduce, modify or update information are restricted according to Annex XIII and the Art. 77(9) implementing act; (g) data authentication, reliability and integrity; (h) a high level of security and privacy and avoidance of fraud.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport systems; responsible economic operators and their service providers
provisions.conditions: No standard or regulation is named in Art. 78 itself. Points (b) and (f) depend on the Art. 77(9) implementing act (not located as adopted). Art. 15(1) lists Art. 78 among the provisions whose verification can rely on harmonised standards.

provisions.summary: The registry arrangements cover batteries covered by Art. 77 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, and 'digital product passport' includes the battery passport. Only verified economic operators may register passports; verification lasts until the electronic identification expires and at most three years. Registration is done through a user interface or API at the level set by the applicable Union law, the most granular level applying where several rules overlap; the registry checks the submission and issues a persistent registration identifier. Operators can generate a sealed proof of registration. Member States appoint a national administrator by 18 February 2027. Entry into force on the twentieth day after publication.

open_questions: When will the Art. 77(9) implementing act be adopted and enter into force, and how will it define persons with a legitimate interest and their download, share, publish and re-use rights for Annex XIII points 2 and 4? As of 2026-10-13 only the Commission FAQ statement that a draft is expected in October or November 2026 was found.
When will the Art. 13(10) labelling implementing act be adopted? Its entry-into-force date plus 18 months fixes the start of the Art. 13(1)-(3) labels.

When will the Art. 7 delegated and implementing acts (carbon footprint methodology, declaration format, performance classes, label format) and the Art. 8(1) recycled-content delegated act be adopted? Their entry into force fixes the start of Annex XIII points 1(c) and 1(e).
Have the Art. 48(5) due diligence guidelines (deadline 26 July 2026) been published? Not located.

What exactly does the agreed text of 2025/0134(COD) (Omnibus IV digitalisation and common specifications) change in Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 - in particular a new Annex XIII point 1(t), digital instructions and the declaration of conformity - and will it be adopted after the plenary forecast for 23 November 2026?
Will 2025/0130(COD) change the EUR 40 million threshold in Art. 47, and will 2025/0397(COD) change Annex VI Part A point 8 (hazardous substances wording) or the producer definition?

Access to Annex XIII point 4 by notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission: Art. 77(2)(b) grants them points 2 and 3 only, and the point 4 heading names only persons with a legitimate interest. Is authority access to individual-battery data intended to flow through market surveillance powers instead?

Who must attribute the unique identifier and keep the passport accurate when a battery is put into service without being placed on the market (own use)? Art. 77(1) and 77(10) cover putting into service, but Art. 77(3) and 77(4) name only the operator placing the battery on the market.

How is 'capacity greater than 2 kWh' to be determined? Art. 3 defines neither capacity nor rated capacity; a footnote on IEC terminology for charge and capacity exists near the annexes but was not read. The Commission FAQ (non-binding) says independently functioning units are assessed individually and integrated systems by combined capacity.

Do batteries placed on the market before 18 February 2027 need a passport when they change status afterwards? The Commission FAQ (non-binding) says a new passport is needed if such a battery is remanufactured after that date; the legal text was not found to address this expressly.

Are the dated ISO/IEC 15459 editions named in Art. 77(3) still current at ISO, and how do EN 18219:2026 and EN 18220:2026 (cited in the OJ under the ESPR by Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736) relate to the 'or their equivalent' wording? The CEN-CENELEC publication status of those EN standards was not checked here.

Art. 77(10) sets no start date for uploading unique identifiers and the registry act's exact entry-into-force date was not read; is registration required before placing on the market from 18 February 2027?
